st_bagages.name: Chemin des Éclaireurs
st_bagages.alt: A sunny country road winding between hedges and green fields, with a wooden bus shelter, a signpost and a reedy pond, painted in ink and gouache: Monsieur Verbe strides away leaving his slice of cake alone on a picnic table; spots a pear on top of the signpost through binoculars; walks a lost duckling back to its mother at the pond; rides a delivery bike piled with packages in a gold beret; kneels to put a toy bus back together; and lounges in an abandoned red armchair on the verge, admiring himself in a hand mirror. The road on the left leads back to the crossroads. The green camper door, the iron farm gate, the stile steps and the arch in the hedge lead on.

doors.label: Jardin des Vacanciers
doors.hint: Through the green door of the camper under the striped canopy

doors.label: Allée des Nouveaux-Voisins
doors.hint: Up the stone steps of the stile

doors.label: Sentier des Lambins
doors.hint: Through the arch in the hedge

vacanciers.name: Jardin des Vacanciers
vacanciers.alt: The garden of a little country guesthouse after a shower, with deckchairs, a tea table and flower pots, and a country bus stopped at the gate: Monsieur Verbe steps off the bus with his suitcase and his pet moose; guides rainwater from the gutter into a flower pot; relaxes in a deckchair with his feet up and a cup of tea; hands his waiter's tray and towel to a cat; lowers his umbrella and points as the sun comes back out, in a gold beret; and, in a gold beret, pulls a cat out of his magician's hat. The stone archway on the left leads back to the road; the guesthouse door leads on.

demenageurs.name: Cour des Déménageurs
demenageurs.alt: Moving day in a farmhouse yard down a country lane, with hay bales in the fields and a removal van with its ramp down: Monsieur Verbe pushes two bushes apart to make room for his handcart; wheels an armchair up the ramp with his clipboard; clanks about in a heavy suit of armor with a gold beret, checking himself in a hand mirror; holds up one red cushion from a pile of white ones in a gold beret; pours his goldfish from a small bowl into a big tank; and dabs happy tears over a letter in a gold beret. The iron gate on the left leads back to the road; the stone archway leads on.

doors.label: Chemin des Éclaireurs
doors.hint: Back through the iron farm gate

voisins.name: Allée des Nouveaux-Voisins
voisins.alt: A small new cottage with a front garden at the edge of green fields, a washing line and a picket fence, under a blazing sun: Monsieur Verbe carries a box inside followed by a parrot, a rabbit and a cat; climbs a ladder to an upstairs window in a gold beret; scratches his head at a cat playing a tuba at the cellar window; walks away from a dusty piano munching a deli sandwich; nearly faints from the heat in a deckchair, fanning himself, in a gold beret; and turns up his nose at a plate of sprouts. The iron gate on the left leads back to the road; the wooden garden gate leads on.

doors.label: Chemin des Éclaireurs
doors.hint: Back through the iron gate at the end of the lane

lambins.name: Sentier des Lambins
lambins.alt: A slow, grassy lane between hedgerows and fields after rain, with puddles, a picnic bench and a huge old oak: Monsieur Verbe weaves his bike back and forth between the puddles; unplugs his laptop at the picnic bench, mirror in hand; jumps back as a tower of old books on a wheelbarrow collapses; puts on his coat and tiptoes away, mirror in hand; crouches with his satchel to watch two snails race on a tree stump; and stands on a crate singing to the pigeons. The arch in the hedge on the left leads back to the road.

doors.label: Chemin des Éclaireurs
doors.hint: Back through the arch in the hedge
